:::{#prp-double-well-divergence}
#### Divergence of gradient descent on the double-well function

Let $f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2$,
and run [gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent)
with a fixed [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $\steplen > 0$.
If $\iterpoint{x}{0}$ satisfies

$$
\iterpoint{x}{0}^2 > 1 + \frac{1}{2\steplen},
$$

then $\abs{\iterpoint{x}{t}} \to \infty$
as $t \to \infty$.

:::

::: proof

The [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) is $\deriv{x} f(x) = 4x^3 - 4x$,
so one step of [gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent) gives

$$
\ba
\iterpoint{x}{t+1}
&= \iterpoint{x}{t} - \steplen\,\paren{4 \iterpoint{x}{t}^3 - 4 \iterpoint{x}{t}}
&& \text{(gradient descent step)}
\\
&= -\iterpoint{x}{t}\,\paren{4\steplen \iterpoint{x}{t}^2 - 4\steplen - 1}.
&& \text{(factor out } -\iterpoint{x}{t} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Write $m(x) \eqdef 4\steplen x^2 - 4\steplen - 1$.
Then $\abs{\iterpoint{x}{t+1}} = \abs{\iterpoint{x}{t}}\, m(\iterpoint{x}{t})$
whenever $m(\iterpoint{x}{t}) \ge 0$.
Now $m(x) > 1$ exactly when $x^2 > 1 + 1 / (2\steplen)$,
and $m(x)$ increases with $x^2$.
So if $\iterpoint{x}{t}$ satisfies the condition,
then $\abs{\iterpoint{x}{t+1}} > \abs{\iterpoint{x}{t}}$,
and $\iterpoint{x}{t+1}$ satisfies it too.
By [induction](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-induction) on $t$,
every iterate satisfies it,
so $\iterpoint{x}{t}^2 \ge \iterpoint{x}{0}^2$ and $m(\iterpoint{x}{t}) \ge m(\iterpoint{x}{0}) > 1$.
Hence $\abs{\iterpoint{x}{t}} \ge m(\iterpoint{x}{0})^t \abs{\iterpoint{x}{0}}$,
which tends to $\infty$.

:::
